families.title: Bayesian and Markov networks
families.intro: Networks against the tools people use for them: Ace 3.0, which compiles a network into an arithmetic circuit, and Merlin 1.7.0's bucket-tree elimination (`-a bte`, and `-t PR` for the partition function), and the other exact network tools: pyAgrum (junction tree), pgmpy (variable elimination), libDAI (junction tree) and TensorInference.jl (tensor network contraction; of its two contraction orders, `treesa` and `greedy`, the faster is shown). On the standard suite's networks, Ace's networks, the large networks and the UAI networks ProbLog, PITA and aspmc ran too. The exact systems that read Dice programs, Dice, Alea.jl, Roulette, noDice, Psi, Genfer, SPPL and Geni, ran on the standard suite's networks, Ace's networks, the large networks and the UAI networks, each network as the Dice program of `scripts/gen_bn.py`, in a later run. tddlog reads a network as a ProbLog program, one annotated disjunction per row of a table.

suites.about: The 120 networks of the UAI 2022 competition's MAR tuning set: tddlog prints the probability of the evidence alone (`--evidence-probability --no-queries`) and Merlin and the other network tools run their partition function tasks; 300 s a run. aspmc, Ace and the Dice family ran in a later run, each instance beside that run's tddlog, which their comparisons use.

setup: Five jobs on four lab machines (36 physical cores and 503 GB; 20 physical cores and 503 GB; 16 physical cores and 251 GB; 16 physical cores and 125 GB), 2026-10-19 to 2026-10-21: every system of a suite in the same job, each run single-threaded and pinned to a physical core of its own, side by side in lanes; Ace in 12 wide lanes of 88 GB, half of it its Java heap. The systems of an instance run in the same lanes, so their times compare. The further systems of a later job (the suites' notes say which) ran in its lanes beside that job's own tddlog, which their comparisons use.

Wall time of the whole process, parsing and grounding included. A system's fastest variant is the one shown: ProbLog's d-DNNF, SDD or forward SDD compilation; Ace's default route or c2d forced. Alea.jl's and Roulette's own times leave out the start-up and compilation of Julia and Racket, as on the page of the Dice family's suites; their processes' wall times are columns of their own.

tddlog 0.1.0 with its default strategy (`auto`), linked statically (tididi e4d60911, goatd e237c1a). Ace 3.0, Merlin 1.7.0, pyAgrum 3.2.1, pgmpy 1.1.2, libDAI 0.3.2, TensorInference.jl, ProbLog 2.3.0, PITA (cplint) and aspmc with sharpSAT-TD. Dice, Alea.jl, Roulette, noDice, Psi, Genfer, SPPL and Geni as on the page of the Dice family's suites.

Every answer of tddlog's, and of each other system, is compared with a reference: the clique tree ([`scripts/bn_exact.py`](https://github.com/Tractables/tddlog/blob/baselines/scripts/bn_exact.py)), Ace or Merlin. The largest absolute differences: 6.3e-15 on Ace's networks, 4.9e-11 on the large networks, 9.1e-14 on the 111 UAI networks the clique tree answers (the other five agree with Merlin's six printed digits); no other system answers Grids_15, Grids_16, Grids_17 and Grids_18. For the partition function tddlog's log10 Z agrees with every other exact answer there is: Merlin's, the clique tree's, or a weighted model count of the network. The other network tools' answers against the same references: pyAgrum 214 marginal runs to 2.0e-7 and 230 partition functions to 2.1e-7 in log10; pgmpy 129 marginal runs to 4.7e-9 and 214 partition functions to 2.2e-7 in log10; libDAI 224 marginal runs to 5.0e-7 and 256 partition functions to 2.2e-7 in log10; TensorInference.jl 341 marginal runs to 5.0e-7 and 380 partition functions to 2.2e-7 in log10 (the tools print six digits, as Merlin does). A baseline's answer off the reference by more than 1e-6 counts as a failure (wrong).

families.title: Probabilistic logic programs
families.intro: Programs in ProbLog's language against ProbLog 2.3.0 (d-DNNF, SDD and forward SDD compilation), PITA's BDDs and aspmc with sharpSAT-TD, and, on TPC-H and the literature suite's pdb and noisy-or, ProvSQL 1.13.0, a PostgreSQL extension that tracks provenance and picks its method for the probability. Scallop's top-k proofs ran too; they are approximate, so their times are in the tables of [docs/benchmarks.md](https://github.com/Tractables/tddlog/blob/baselines/docs/benchmarks.md) and not here. On the standard suite, the literature suite, TPC-H and Biomine, Ace, Merlin, the other network tools and the exact systems that read Dice programs, Dice, Alea.jl, Roulette, noDice, Psi, Genfer, SPPL and Geni, ran on the network and the Dice program that [`scripts/ground2net.py`](https://github.com/Tractables/tddlog/blob/baselines/scripts/ground2net.py) writes of a program's ground program, in a later run.

suites.title: Standard suite: programs
suites.about: 50 programs: random graphs, grids, smokers, UW-CSE, Cora citation matching, blood types and the Dice paper's programs translated to ProbLog; 300 s a run. aspmc, Ace, Merlin, pyAgrum, pgmpy, libDAI, TensorInference.jl and the Dice family ran in a later run, each instance beside that run's tddlog, which their comparisons use.

suites.title: Literature suite
suites.about: 39 programs of six families from published evaluations (mnist_sum, pedigree, sickness, noisy-or, mastermind, pdb), each grown on a random structure from a seed; 300 s a run. ProvSQL ran on the two tuple-independent families, pdb and noisy-or (the others are recursive or have annotated disjunctions), in a later run on another machine, each instance beside tddlog: its times compare with that run's tddlog, which its comparison uses. aspmc, Ace, Merlin, pyAgrum, pgmpy, libDAI, TensorInference.jl and the Dice family ran in a later run, each instance beside that run's tddlog, which their comparisons use.

suites.title: TPC-H
suites.about: The TPC-H queries as Boolean queries over a tuple-independent database, at scale factors 0.001 to 0.1, flat and through views (208 instances); 600 s a run. Ace, Merlin, pyAgrum, pgmpy, libDAI, TensorInference.jl and the Dice family ran in a later run, each instance beside that run's tddlog, which their comparisons use.

suites.title: Biomine
suites.about: The probability that each of four genes is connected to Alzheimer disease in the human Biomine network, over the union of the K most probable paths, for ten values of K up to 64; 600 s a run. Ace, Merlin, pyAgrum, pgmpy, libDAI, TensorInference.jl and the Dice family ran in a later run, each instance beside that run's tddlog, which their comparisons use.

setup: Three jobs on two lab machines (36 and 20 physical cores, 503 GB each), 2026-10-19 to 2026-10-20: every system of a suite in the same job, each run single-threaded and pinned to a physical core of its own, side by side in lanes; Ace in 12 wide lanes of 88 GB, half of it its Java heap. The systems of an instance run in the same lanes, so their times compare. The further systems of a later job (the suites' notes say which) ran in its lanes beside that job's own tddlog, which their comparisons use.

Wall time of the whole process, parsing and grounding included. A system's fastest variant is the one shown: ProbLog's d-DNNF, SDD or forward SDD compilation; Ace's default route or c2d forced. Alea.jl's and Roulette's own times leave out the start-up and compilation of Julia and Racket, as on the page of the Dice family's suites; their processes' wall times are columns of their own.

tddlog 0.1.0 with its default strategy (`auto`), linked statically (tididi e4d60911, goatd e237c1a). ProbLog 2.3.0, PITA (cplint) and aspmc with sharpSAT-TD; ProvSQL 1.13.0 on PostgreSQL 16.4. Ace 3.0, Merlin 1.7.0, pyAgrum 3.2.1, pgmpy 1.1.2, libDAI 0.3.2 and TensorInference.jl. Dice, Alea.jl, Roulette, noDice, Psi, Genfer, SPPL and Geni as on the page of the Dice family's suites.

Every answer of tddlog's is compared with a reference: ProbLog's, or an exact solver written for the suite ([`scripts/lit_exact.py`](https://github.com/Tractables/tddlog/blob/baselines/scripts/lit_exact.py), [`scripts/tpch_exact.py`](https://github.com/Tractables/tddlog/blob/baselines/scripts/tpch_exact.py), [`scripts/reliability_exact.py`](https://github.com/Tractables/tddlog/blob/baselines/scripts/reliability_exact.py)). The largest absolute differences: 4.9e-9 on the standard suite (ProbLog prints eight digits), 2.7e-13 on the literature suite, 1.0e-14 on TPC-H, 3.4e-12 on Biomine; ProvSQL's answers differ from the reference's by at most 1.0e-12 on TPC-H and by at most 8.9e-16 on pdb and noisy-or. The random graphs and grids no exact system finishes agree with estimates from sampled graphs ([`scripts/sample_paths.py`](https://github.com/Tractables/tddlog/blob/baselines/scripts/sample_paths.py)). A baseline's answer off the reference by more than 1e-6 counts as a failure (wrong).
